gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 26?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 26 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

These stable conditions, driven by a weak high-pressure ridge and no strong frontal systems, support the market’s leading implied probabilities for the 27°C (46.5%) and 26°C (32.5%) outcomes. Current runs sit slightly above the long-term August average high of 23.1°C but remain well below historical extremes above 30°C. Updated model guidance and any late adjustments to cloud cover or advection will determine the final official reading used for market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from models like ECMWF and ICON place Munich's August 27 peak temperature near 29–30 °C under a stable high-pressure regime with light easterly flow, partly cloudy skies, and negligible precipitation risk. Minor model spread arises from differences in afternoon cloud cover and boundary-layer mixing, which can shift the daily maximum by 1–2 °C; drier, clearer solutions support 31–32 °C while increased high cloud or slightly stronger winds favor 28–29 °C. Historical late-August climatology in Munich centers around 24–26 °C, so current guidance reflects a modest warm anomaly. Market odds clustered at 30–31 °C reflect this tight consensus amid typical short-range forecast uncertainty.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on August 27 centers on uncertainty in short-range forecast models amid an incoming weather system.** Official guidance from the Met Office and other sources shows a transition from warm, humid conditions on August 25 (highs near 22–24°C) to more unsettled weather, with yellow thunderstorm warnings and spells of heavy rain or showers expected through Thursday.

Key differentiating factors include cloud cover versus sunny intervals, which will determine whether daytime heating reaches 25–26°C or stays capped near 24°C. Easterly or southeasterly winds, high dew points near 17–18°C, and potential for persistent low cloud or precipitation (30–80% chance in some runs) are expected to moderate temperatures. Ensemble forecasts diverge slightly on the timing and intensity of showers, creating the narrow spread between the leading 24°C (33.5%) and 25°C (32.5%) outcomes, while lower probabilities for 26°C or below 24°C reflect the limited upside from Atlantic moisture and the downside risk from widespread cloud.

Upcoming Met Office and ECMWF model updates, plus any observed changes in steering flow, will likely refine these probabilities before resolution.

**Recent official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and supporting models indicate a transition to cloudier, showery conditions over Tokyo on August 27, moderating peak temperatures relative to the prior hot spell.** 

JMA guidance points to a maximum near 31°C with frequent scattered showers and 50-60% precipitation probability, while other numerical models and outlooks cluster in the 30–33°C range amid high humidity and southerly flow. The primary driver is an approaching low-pressure system and frontal boundary, which increases cloud cover, limits daytime insolation, and introduces evaporative cooling from rain—factors that differentiate the tightly bunched 30–32°C market outcomes. 

Earlier clear, sunny conditions on August 25–26 allowed readings to reach 35°C, but the shift to overcast skies and afternoon/evening thunderstorms is expected to cap the daily high. Minor variations in shower timing, cloud thickness, or model consensus on the low’s track could nudge the outcome by 1–2°C, consistent with the close market-implied probabilities around these levels. Updated JMA briefings and short-range model runs on the morning of the 27th will provide the clearest resolution signals for traders.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 27 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts from authoritative sources like the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), Japan Times, and international models converge on a peak temperature of 33–34°C for Tokyo on August 26, 2026, aligning closely with the market's leading implied probabilities (34°C at 48.5%, 33°C at 25.5%, and 35°C at 21.0%).**

Late-summer conditions in the region feature high humidity, southerly flows, and the urban heat island effect amplifying daytime maxima, while scattered afternoon thunderstorms or increased cloud cover introduce modest cooling potential that caps upside risk. Recent JMA guidance and model runs indicate mainly clear to partly cloudy skies with isolated showers possible later in the day, supporting a most-likely high near 34°C (roughly 93°F). Historical climatology for late August shows typical peaks around 30–32°C, so current conditions reflect above-average warmth without extreme heatwave dynamics. 

Traders appear to weight the consensus central tendency from official forecasts most heavily, with smaller probabilities on 35°C reflecting residual model spread and the chance of clearer conditions allowing an extra degree or two. Resolution will depend on the official JMA daily maximum recorded at the Tokyo station.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble models point to a Tokyo high of 30–32°C on August 27, driven by the strengthening Pacific subtropical high that favors clear to partly cloudy skies and light winds, with limited sea-breeze cooling. Market-implied odds cluster tightly around these values because short-range guidance shows only modest spread in maximum temperatures, reflecting uncertainty over afternoon cloud development and exact dew-point levels rather than major synoptic shifts. Historical late-August baselines average near 31°C, so traders are pricing the narrow window where small forecast revisions could shift resolution between the three leading outcomes. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will provide the next key data point for refining probabilities.
